claims.text: Ion irradiation introduces lattice defects in bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Ion irradiation could reduce the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Irradiation-induced lattice defects mediate the proposed reduction in lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed reduction applies over 0 to 200 K.
Increasing ion-irradiation dose is expected to decrease thermal conductivity.

contradictions.description: The prediction concerns the lattice contribution specifically, but the falsification rule uses total thermal conductivity. Total conductivity could remain unchanged or increase because of an electronic contribution even if the lattice contribution decreases, so this rule does not decisively test the stated hypothesis.

The conditions specify room temperature, whereas the prediction boundary is 0 to 200 K. This could mean room-temperature irradiation followed by low-temperature measurement, but that distinction is not stated.
